text:
maya: heads up - aurora21b-int4 on shared-dedicated saw a memory spike and 2 OOMs during a multi-tenant ramp at 02:07. suspect tenant A + tenant B both triggering prefetch heavy requests.
ops-bot: alert: cluster=ded-3 task=aurora21b-canary reason=OOM_kv_reserve hosts=[a2-08,a2-09]
trent: can you grab the thin repro and current defaults? curious about per-request cap and max_new_tokens.
maya: repro snippet below: 
```
[02:07:02] config: prefetch_window=40 prefetch_slots=4 max_new_tokens=384 batch=20
[02:07:02] tenant=A request: alloc_kv 9.6GB -> total_reserved 38.9GB
[02:07:03] tenant=B request: alloc_kv 8.2GB -> total_reserved 47.1GB
[02:07:04] OOM allocating 2.8GB for kv_prefetch
```
jax: interesting - our per-request prefetch is unbounded across tenants. we multiply by batch and slots and then sum. two concurrent tenant spikes can easily crush the free pool.
ben: quick local bench: baseline (defaults above) peak=52.4GB OOMs=2. change 1: cap per-request_prefetch_bytes=6GB -> peak=36.8GB OOMs=0. change 2: lower max_new_tokens=128 -> peak=34.5GB OOMs=0 but p95 latency +40ms.
maya: run with cap + gradual prefetch (initial_prefetch=0 ramp_to=2 over 3 requests) looks promising.
ops-bot: bench requested by maya: `bench --model aurora21b --runs 250 --batch 12 --max-new 128 --prefetch-cap 6GB --prefetch-mode gradual`
ops-bot: bench result: peak_gpu_mem=34.5GB avg_latency=76ms p95=215ms OOMs=0 (prev peak=52.4GB OOMs=2). artifacts s3://redwood-ci/aurora21b/1787654322/canary.
trent: QA note: we need to check quantization quality with reduced max_new_tokens on long-form summarization and multi-turn codegen. @qa-bot schedule eval.
qa-bot: eval scheduled: aurora21b/int4/2026-03-15-1787654322. CSVs to /evals/aurora21b/1787654322.
jax: proposal for canary config diff: 
```
models:
  aurora21b:
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 128
      prefetch_window: 12
      prefetch_slots: 2
      per_request_prefetch_cap_bytes: 6442450944  # 6GB
      prefetch_mode: gradual
      prefetch_ramp_requests: 3
      batch: 12
      slot_compactor: soft_start
```
ben: also adding runtime guard: when free_kv_pool < threshold, refuse prefetch and fallback to on-demand per-token fetch. prevents multi-tenant cascading OOMs. we can ship as a runtime flag `prefetch_global_cap=true`.
maya: plan: 1) PR with config + runtime guard + metrics (kv_reserved_peak, per_tenant_prefetch) 2) canary 10% eu-west for 6 hours across two pools 3) run eval + perf bench 4) if stable, expand to 50% then GA. tagging @oncall-infra for tracing hooks.
trent: one more ask: add a regression alert for any metric delta >1.5% on our core evals for codegen and summarization.
maya: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/4293 - CI running. attaching bench logs to the PR. :rocket:
ops-bot: CI passed, canary deploy started. watching memory and per-tenant prefetch metrics.
maya: follow-up after 2h: canary steady, no OOMs, kv_reserved_peak reduced ~35%. QA evals showing rouge down 0.4%, codegen EM unchanged. will keep thread updated.
